# Animated roster sorting moves cards twice before settling

## Context and problem

Operator report, 2026-10-13, in the running Fleet Manager: switching the roster cards between **Online first** and **Name** produces two visible moves. Cards first travel to an apparent default/unsorted arrangement, wait for that transition, then travel to the requested order. The operator reports this on changes generally; the sort switch is the concrete reproducer.

Expected: one sort intent moves surviving cards directly from their displayed positions to the requested order. Installed candidate/pins and a recorded frame timeline have not yet been captured. Store clearing and the intermediate arrangement being genuinely “unsorted” are hypotheses, not observed Store facts.

## Architectural reality

Current source checked at Engine `fe6ab42c75675a007bd9d7390fdc09afb4493f74` and Institution `e5aa4238b7acba14ec5383bfd300ce2f2b8e8af2`:

1. Institution `apps/agentos/view/fleet/roster/Controller.mjs:166–177` replaces `store.sorters` once. It does not clear/refill the Store.
2. Engine `src/data/Store.mjs:1269–1274` emits coarse `load` during `sort`. This is intentional; #16559 / #16616 preserve load-only consumers.
3. `src/list/Base.mjs:387–392,623–648,878–886` binds both events; the load handler synchronously rebuilds VDOM in current Store order.
4. `src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs:739–770` then maps `previousItems` indices onto `vdom.cn`, assuming those nodes still have the previous order. Its timer at `:777–784` calls `createItems()` after `transitionDuration` (default 500 ms).

This sequence strongly explains an incorrect first target followed by a settlement correction. It is source evidence, **not an independent rendered reproduction**.

Design authority: the roster List's JSDoc says “a sort MOVES the surviving instances (translate transition)”; #17553 requires stable cards without rebuilding/flashing. The operator identifies the intermediate detour as a defect. Institution's record-keyed pool/DOM identity from #99 must remain intact.

## The fix

First capture the event/record/node/transform timeline on the ordinary Store → animated component-list path. Correct ownership of the sort presentation in the shared list/Animate layer so it uses the actual displayed identity/order and settlement does not launch another visible move. Do not suppress Store's documented load-on-sort contract or add a Fleet-only timer workaround.

## Contract ledger

| Surface | Authority / behavior | Edge and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Animated component-list sort | Store owns order; List/Animate owns presentation. One direct movement of retained cards to that order. | Repeated sorts and a sort during motion; rendered timeline, stable nodes/focus/selection. |
| Store load-on-sort | Existing #16559 contract remains unchanged. | Load-only consumers and ordinary non-sort loads still update; existing contract controls. |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce a genuine reorder with at least three differently ordered records, in both sort directions, through the real Store event path. Retain a pre-fix timeline distinguishing Store order, VDOM/node identity and painted positions; bind the rendering environment.
- [ ] One sort produces one direct animated movement to its final order, with no intermediate wrong target or delayed second leg. Repeated and in-flight sort changes settle at the latest requested order without a stale timer restoring an older layout.
- [ ] Existing card/list DOM identities, keyboard focus and selection survive. Ordinary loads, filter/join/leave behavior and reduced motion remain correct; Store's coarse/fine notification contract is preserved.
- [ ] A visible component/browser regression covers motion across the settlement boundary, not merely final ordering. Run the applicable explicit Neo test config.

## Scope and follow-through

One shared animation repair; no roster data model, backend, release scheduling or general redesign. Do not disable animation, lengthen sleeps, or weaken the final-order assertion to hide the detour.

Fleet installed revalidation after the corrected Engine pin ships belongs to neomjs/neo-agent-institution#505 / #12: repeat Online first ↔ Name on the installed roster and record candidate/pins. An Engine source merge alone is not that receipt.

Related: #16559, #16538, #17553, #17552; neomjs/neo-agent-institution#99 and #285 cover different identity/reconcile defects.

# Animated component-list sorting evidence

`animated-sort-before-name-asc.json` and `animated-sort-before-name-desc.json`
retain the pre-fix observation at Engine `95e058fed96238c9afe5c06f363321458810be23`.
Each file binds the production source hashes, Chromium version, viewport and
sampling mode. The capture used the record-keyed list in the sibling
`apps/animated-sort` fixture; the later fixture also exercises an index-pooled
list. Node 25.9.0 launched the original capture; validation of the repair used
the supported Node 24.19.0 runtime.

`before`, `afterIntent` and `after` are App Worker observations: Store order,
wrapper transform targets and card construction identities. `frames` records
`getBoundingClientRect()` positions sampled through both transition intervals.
Its `columns` array defines each value; coordinate suffixes refer to the
corresponding entry in `nodeIds`. A mask bit set at index N means that node N
remained connected or was still the same DOM object. All five bits set is 31.
Coordinates and milliseconds are rounded to 0.001; identity masks are exact.
`rawSha256` identifies the original full capture, not this compact JSON.
The sampling clock starts before the click. Rectangles describe the browser's
interpolated positions; inline transforms describe requested targets. Endpoint
screenshots are separate from the motion samples.

The ascending trace shows a wrong target followed by a second painted leg.
The descending trace has collinear motion: its wrong initial target and delayed
correction are visible in `afterIntent` versus `after`, so a straight-path check
alone cannot detect that case. The regression checks both the requested targets
and the painted path across settlement.

From the repository root, with a supported Node runtime and dependencies:

```sh
npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/list/AnimateSort.spec.mjs
```

The explicit component configuration serves this checkout. The spec attaches
new ASC, DESC and interrupted-sort JSON captures and before/after screenshots
to the Playwright result. Those captures bind the tested production hashes.
This is isolated Engine browser evidence; installed Fleet revalidation belongs
to the existing Institution acceptance work.
